test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Picnics are Grasses.

All Grasses Are Rains.

Some Rains are Clouds.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Grasses are Clouds.

(II) All Picnics are Rains.
solution:
Given Statements:

Some Picnics are Grasses.

All Grasses Are Rains.

Some Rains are Clouds.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements are:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/209bea963bcd5db9885e427d1ac00118727d53df2726d3090b9778031a8b5dd2.png] 

Conclusions:

I) Some Grasses are clouds → **FALSE** (There is no definite relation given between grass and clouds, so it is a possible only).

II) All Picnics are Rains →** FALSE** (Some Picnic are definitely Rains, but All Picnics are Rains can be possibly only).

So, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

Hence the correct answer is** "Option 4".**
